meaning: Engulf weather reading: each day's forecast against past years, and what it means.
lead: 9 days away. Forecasts this far ahead are rough, so treat these as best guesses. This page updates twice a day.
banner: This is preliminary until about Nov 7, when the hour-by-hour forecast for burn night comes in. It gets more accurate the closer we get to the burn.
summary: Expect afternoons around 74°, nights around 53°, and a chance of a shower or two. Day: T-shirt. Night: long sleeves.
Burn night looks like light wind (around 6 mph), probably dry, and about 58° at the burns. Night: fleece.

A normal Engulf week: afternoons around 72°, nights around 45°. It rains on about 1 in 7 days, frost comes about 1 in 10 nights, and wind at burn time rarely reaches 15 mph. Day: T-shirt. Night: warm jacket, hat, gloves; winter layers in a cold year.
When you'll know more: the hour-by-hour forecast for burn night starts around Nov 7; from about Nov 11, three days out, forecasts are usually within a few degrees.
why: The latest forecasts from the European and US weather services make up 69% to 88% of each day's numbers. This far out they're rough, so the rest is what a normal Engulf week looks like, from 30 years of records.
NOAA's longer-range outlook leans clearly warmer than normal for Nov 11–17, so the normal-year part of every day is nudged that way.
The last month ran warm and dry, but that says little about any single day a week or more out, so it isn't in the numbers.
Each update leans more on the forecast; from a week out it's all forecast.
